Proposal only. No compute has been started.

**Why there is no CPU smoke check.** The BEND run guide (`discovery-benchmark-bend`, revision `ac6e80c75e09d83cf47a7b4bcf0e44599c5706cf`) does three things:
1. Downloads the whole data share with `scripts/download_bend.py`.
2. Precomputes ResNetLM and AWD-LSTM embeddings for two tasks.
3. Trains and evaluates gene finding.

The guide offers no reduced-input path, and the download script takes the whole share. Measured on 2026-11-17 by crawling the share the script reads and sending a HEAD request for each file:
- 29 files, 7,251,859,341 bytes in total.
- `data/genomes` is 6.35 GB of that. It includes `GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa` (3,151,417,447 bytes) and `GRCh37.no-chr.fa` (3,199,905,630 bytes).
- `data/gene_finding` is 0.36 GB.

`download_bend.py` holds each response in memory (`r.content`) before writing it, so the largest genome file implies more than 3 GB of RAM. This is inferred from the script and the file size, not measured.

The embedding step runs both language models over every sequence of `gene_finding` and `enhancer_annotation`. Its CPU time is not stated anywhere and was not measured.

**Estimated cost of a full run: unknown.**
- Measured basis: 7.25 GB download. Inferred, not measured: more than 3.2 GB peak RAM in the download step.
- Compute: no basis. The guide says no hardware, runtime or cost is stated in the README.

Pilot to measure it: run only `precompute_embeddings.py model=resnetlm task=gene_finding` on one GPU with timing, then extrapolate to both models and both tasks before deciding on the full run.

Refs #61
title: Proposal: BEND gene-finding full run (7.25 GB data, embedding precompute)

In CI on ubuntu-24.04 (run https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire-benchmarks/actions/runs/44124569152, job `massspecgym`):

- `conda create -n massspecgym python==3.11` then `pip install massspecgym` resolved `massspecgym==1.3.1`. The install is unpinned, as the guide notes.
- The tutorial script stops at its third line, `import pytorch_lightning as pl`:

```
File ".../site-packages/lightning_fabric/__init__.py", line 41, in <module>
    __import__("pkg_resources").declare_namespace(__name__)
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pkg_resources'
```

The resolved `pytorch-lightning==2.2.5` (with `torch==2.3.0`) imports `pkg_resources`, which is not present in the environment. setuptools 81 and later no longer ship it; `pip freeze` does not list the setuptools version, so that cause is likely but not confirmed. The smoke check would only pass by changing the documented install, for example by pinning `setuptools<81` or a newer Lightning. That is a recipe change, so it was left out of #61's CI.

**Suggested next step.** Decide on a pinned install (a lock file, or `massspecgym` plus `setuptools<81`) and update the run guide. The CPU smoke job can then be added back. A draft exists in the history of PR #66 (`scripts/recipe_smoke/massspecgym.sh`). It limits the Trainer to 1 epoch and 20/5/5 batches.

**Estimated cost of the full tutorial run: unknown.**
- It is a CPU tutorial: 5 epochs, batch size 32, no GPU.
- It downloads `MassSpecGym.tsv` (262,334,768 bytes) and `MassSpecGym_retrieval_candidates_mass.json` (454,710,480 bytes), with sizes from the Hugging Face API on 2026-11-17.

FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/home/runner/.cache/ProteinGym/zero_shot_substitutions_scores/EVmutation/B2L11_HUMAN_Dutta_2010_binding-Mcl-1.csv'

Clinical labs use computational evidence through ClinGen's calibrated PP3/BP4 thresholds, not leaderboards. A calibration of genomic foundation model scores in that framework would give labs something they can use and cite. It is also a natural paper (see the publishing triage issue).

## Change
Calibrate a small set of Tier 1 model scores for PP3/BP4 evidence strength, following Pejaver et al. 2022 (PMC9748256) and the 2025 follow-up that calibrated AlphaMissense, ESM1b and VARITY.

- **Models:** start with two or three whose precomputed scores we can obtain without GPU runs, such as GPN-MSA and Evo 2 published scores, against SpliceAI, CADD and AlphaMissense as references.
- **Variants:** ClinVar 2-star-or-better P/LP and B/LB, held out from each model's training where known. Use the gnomAD-correction lessons from #53 and #54.
- **Output:**
  - thresholds for each evidence strength, with intervals;
  - the share of variants reaching each strength;
  - receipts for every input.
- **GPU:** none needed for precomputed scores. Any model that needs a GPU run becomes a priced proposal for Tim.

## Done when
Calibrated thresholds for at least two genomic models, with receipts, are in the database, and a draft outline is in the publishing triage.
title: Calibrate genomic model scores for ClinGen PP3/BP4 evidence strength

## Question

The AMP rare-disease case test found a possible gain at rank 1 when GPN-MSA is added to the combined lookup scores: about 6 points at Top-1. The talk showed it as "possible gain at rank 1, to confirm". Does the gain hold on an independent held-out set of cases?

## What exists

- The case construction and results are in rewire-bio/amp-2026-studies, under `docs/rare-disease/` and `docs/rare-disease-v2/`. Check whether `docs/rare-disease-v2/figures/top1_by_group_replication.png` already answers this before building anything new.
- The original design drew 200 diagnostic ClinVar 2-star-or-better P/LP SNVs (60 missense, 40 canonical splice, 30 nonsense, 70 synonymous/UTR/intronic) and placed them in 50 1000 Genomes backgrounds (seed 20261016).
- CADD v1.7, SpliceAI, REVEL, AlphaMissense, GPN-MSA and GPN-Star are all precomputed lookups, so no GPU is needed.
- #53 and #54 (moved from amp-2026-studies) found that the background people are in gnomAD, which flatters the frequency signal. Any replication must use the corrected frequency filter from #54.

## Done when

- A held-out cohort of non-overlapping ClinVar P/LP SNVs, 500 to 1,000 cases, has been run against the locked "lookups combined" model and the "lookups + GPN-MSA" model.
- The Top-1 difference is reported with an interval.
- The result goes into rewire-benchmark-data as an evaluation, and the database shows it.

body:
A second run of the rare-disease case tests, to fix the problems found in the v17 review of the talk, with a smaller scope. Depends on rewire-bio/rewire-benchmarks#53.

## What the talk uses

Only `rare-disease/` needs to change. `evee/`, `gpu-drift/`, `evo2-pipeline/` and `brca1-case-ranking/` are not affected.

| Study part | Results | Used by the talk for |
|---|---|---|
| SNVs, 200 cases | `results.json` | The main case test, by variant type and combined |
| Replication, 500 new cases | `results_replication.json` | Whether the gains hold with the same model, unchanged |
| gnomAD filters | `results*_gnomad0.001*.json` | The frequency-filter check |
| Indels, 120 cases | `results_indel*.json` | The Evo 2 gain on indels |
| Inherited cancer panel, 140 cases | `results_cancer.json` | Ranking, and the PP3 classification test |
| AVI on held-out chromosomes | `avi_heldout.json` | The check against AVI's training data |

## Problems to fix

1. **The background people are in gnomAD** (#1). Every background SNV is in gnomAD and 75% of spiked-in SNVs are not, so frequency is a far stronger signal than in a real patient. For indels it is 99% of background against 30% of spiked-in.
2. **The realistic frequency filter is treated as a side check.** README.md and REPLICATION.md call the overall-AF filter (gnomAD AF below 0.1%) the one "a pipeline would apply". Published pipelines filter per ancestry group: the Genomics England rare disease tiering applies its thresholds per population, and Exomiser compares the cutoff against each gnomAD sub-population. That is the grpmax filter, where AVI shows no clear gain (locked, 500 cases: +0.2, -3.6 to +3.8).
3. **The combined model is a weak baseline within each variant type.** On the 200 cases at top 1 it loses to the matching single tool in every type: canonical splice 82% against SpliceAI 90%, nonsense 60% against CADD 90%, missense 43% against REVEL or AlphaMissense 58%. The replication shows the same. Part of what an added score gains may make up for the model.
4. **Two consequence annotations.** The spiked-in variants are grouped by ClinVar's MC field (most severe across transcripts), while the model's classes come from CADD, whose "splice" class also takes splice-region variants. A variant can be in one group in the results and a different class in the model.
5. **Small groups.** With 30 to 70 cases per type, most per-type differences are noise (nonsense swings from -3 to +32 points across runs). Report paired intervals for every gain, and draw them as dot-and-interval charts, not bars with error bars.

## Scope of the rerun

1. **Build the realistic filter into the design.** Use gnomAD frequencies without the 1000 Genomes samples (#1). Keep a background variant only if it is below 0.1% in every grpmax group, as a dominant-model pipeline would. This replaces the unfiltered, overall 0.1% and grpmax variants with one result per study. Keep one grpmax run at 1% as the recessive-mode check.
2. **Fewer scores.** The four lookups (CADD v1.7, SpliceAI, REVEL, AlphaMissense) and AlphaGenome AVI. Evo 2 is left out of this run and can be added later (see the comment below). Drop GPN-Star-V and GPN-Star-M, which the talk only mentions in the companion.
3. **One consequence annotation** for choosing the spiked-in variants, for the model and for the reported groups: CADD's for SNVs, `annotate_indels.py` for indels. No VEP needed.
4. **Two baselines.** The combined lookups as now, and a rule-based one that scores each variant with the tool for its type: SpliceAI for splice, REVEL or AlphaMissense for missense, CADD for the rest. Report the gain from adding AVI or Evo 2 against both.
5. **Keep the 200 + 500 design.** Fix the analysis before looking at the 500, fit on the 200 and apply the same model, unchanged, to the 500.
6. **Indels: keep**, without Evo 2 at first. They are the only place Evo 2 matters to the talk; whether to run it on the frozen indel cases is decided after this run.
7. **Cancer panel: keep the PP3 test, drop the ranking test.** Ranking is easy with a median of 17 candidates (lookups 85 to 88% top 1). The PP3 test compares score distributions and can be recomputed from the existing scores.
8. **Held-out chromosomes check: keep**, rerun on the new results.

## Cost

CPU only. A later Evo 2 run on the frozen indel cases would be a small job on one H100 (the first run scored 13,345 variants in 2 h 50 min for about USD 11).

## Open questions

- GPN-MSA: keep it as one line (its gain did not replicate) or drop it.
- Cancer ranking: confirm it can go.

## Done when

- `results/` holds one result per study with the realistic filter, both baselines and paired intervals.
- README.md and REPLICATION.md describe the new design, its limits, and what changed from the first run and why.
- The charts are redrawn as dot-and-interval charts.
- A new tag for the talk to cite.
title: Rerun the rare-disease case tests with a realistic frequency filter and a smaller scope

body:
## Problem

The case backgrounds come from 1000 Genomes, and the 1000 Genomes samples are part of gnomAD. So every background variant has been seen in gnomAD at least once, while most spiked-in ClinVar variants have not.

gnomAD genome frequency (`data/gnomad_af.tsv`) of the variants in each case set:

| Variants | n | Not in gnomAD | Below 0.01% | 0.01 to 0.1% | 0.1% or more |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200 cases, spiked-in | 200 | 75% | 24% | 2% | 0% |
| 200 cases, background | 13,145 | 0% | 17% | 26% | 57% |
| 500 cases, spiked-in | 500 | 76% | 23% | 1% | 0% |
| 500 cases, background | 11,208 | 0% | 15% | 29% | 56% |

In about three quarters of cases, "not in gnomAD" on its own singles out the spiked-in variant.

A real patient is not in gnomAD. Their private, very rare background variants are also absent from it, and they compete with the causal variant. Our backgrounds have none of these competitors, so the test makes frequency a much stronger signal than it is in practice.

## What it affects

- Any score that has learned population frequency. AlphaGenome AVI was trained on gnomAD frequency classes, which may explain why it is the best single score and why its gain over the lookups disappears under the grpmax filter.
- The gnomAD-filtered results (`--gnomad-max-af`, with and without `--grpmax`). After the filter, the remaining background variants are still all in gnomAD, so the lists are easier than a real patient's. The lookups' 74 to 80% top 1 under grpmax may be too high.
- Possibly conservation-based scores as well, since conservation and rarity are correlated.

The design limits in README.md and REPLICATION.md do not mention this.

## Proposed fix

1. Compute gnomAD frequencies without the 1000 Genomes samples. gnomAD v3.1.2 reports the HGDP + 1000 Genomes subset separately; check whether its allele counts can be subtracted from the full counts, per group as well as overall.
2. Rewrite `gnomad_af.py` to record the frequency without 1000 Genomes, and treat a background variant that is then absent as not found (AF 0), as a pipeline would.
3. Rerun the frequency filters and the case tests (`case_benchmark.py`, all studies), and the charts.
4. Add the result, and this limit, to README.md and REPLICATION.md.

No GPU is needed. Do this before the other open study changes: a rule-based baseline per consequence, one consequence annotation for everything, and the frequency-filter write-up. Their numbers depend on it.

## How to reproduce the table

```sh
cd rare-disease/data
python3 - <<'EOF'
import csv
af = {(r["chrom"], r["pos"], r["ref"], r["alt"]): r
      for r in csv.DictReader(open("gnomad_af.tsv"), delimiter="\t")}
for name, path in [("200 cases", "cases.tsv"), ("500 cases", "replication/cases.tsv")]:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(path), delimiter="\t"))
    for lab in ("1", "0"):
        keys = {(r["chrom"], r["pos"], r["ref"], r["alt"]) for r in rows if r["diagnostic"] == lab}
        a = [(af[k]["gnomad_found"] == "True", float(af[k]["gnomad_af"])) for k in keys if k in af]
        n = len(a)
        absent = sum(not f for f, x in a)
        print(name, "spiked-in" if lab == "1" else "background", n, f"not in gnomAD {100 * absent / n:.0f}%")
EOF
```
title: Background people are in gnomAD, so the frequency signal is flattered

body:
## Proposed follow-up study

Test whether Evo 2 sequence-likelihood changes and AlphaGenome predicted expression effects agree on the **same variants**, and whether either adds useful information about measured regulatory effects.

Status: idea for scoping, not an executed study or an established correlation. Tim requested that this be recorded in rewire-database on 20 October 2026.

### Motivation

A reader asked whether Evo 2 likelihood scores line up with AlphaGenome expression predictions or are essentially uncorrelated:
https://www.reddit.com/r/ArtificialInteligence/comments/1x9uvz5/comment/phuo6yf/

Our reply clarifies that no paired result is being reported:
https://www.reddit.com/r/ArtificialInteligence/comments/1x9uvz5/comment/phv2rn9/

Related guide: https://rewirebio.io/blog/genomic-foundation-models-in-the-diagnostic-lab/

### Suggested pilot to scope

- Choose a public regulatory-variant dataset with quantitative experimental effects and a defensible match to AlphaGenome tissue/cell-type expression outputs. Check licences, coverage and possible training overlap before choosing the dataset.
- Freeze a common variant set, genome assembly, reference/alternate alleles, target genes and applicable tissues. Record exclusions and missing predictions.
- Predeclare the Evo 2 checkpoint, context, strand handling, likelihood aggregation and sign convention. Predeclare AlphaGenome version, expression tracks and variant-effect scorer. Keep signed effects and effect magnitudes separate: sequence plausibility is not an expression direction.
- Compare paired scores using rank correlation and uncertainty intervals, with locus-aware resampling where variants are dependent. Examine tissue/gene and variant-class strata rather than relying only on a pooled correlation.
- Separately evaluate agreement with experimental measurements. Model-to-model agreement alone does not establish biological accuracy; low agreement alone does not establish complementarity.
- If justified by pilot size and coverage, assess whether combining scores improves held-out prediction over either score and a simple baseline. Use gene/locus-separated evaluation and prevent tuning on the test set.
- Record inference cost, memory, missingness and reproducible score tables alongside results. Do not promise a full run until feasibility and compute are scoped.

### Initial deliverables

- [ ] Review existing paired comparisons and identify the evidence gap.
- [ ] Select a suitable dataset and write a short preregistered pilot protocol.
- [ ] Establish feasible access, licensing and compute costs.
- [ ] Run the pilot only after a separate execution decision.
- [ ] Report effect sizes, uncertainty, limitations and reusable artifacts, including a null result if warranted.

### Repository placement

This issue records the idea in rewire-database as requested. Its README assigns benchmark execution to rewire-benchmarks and reviewed scientific records to rewire-benchmark-data; link implementation and evidence work there if the study proceeds. Do not add speculative results to the catalogue.

Primary implementation references to review during scoping:
- https://github.com/ArcInstitute/evo2
- https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphagenome
title: Proposed study: paired Evo 2 likelihood and AlphaGenome expression effects

body:
Part of #30. Data case: rewire-bio/rewire-benchmark-data#18 (`diagnostic-genomics-model-execution`). Article: [What published benchmarks show about accelerating variant calling and genomic models](https://rewirebio.io/blog/what-published-benchmarks-show-about-accelerating-variant-calling-and-genomic-models/).

## Why

No study reruns a variant-calling pipeline on the same input and compares the calls. No study prints accuracy in the same table as runtime and memory for the same runs. Hardware differs within almost every comparison. Genomic foundation model execution is owned elsewhere (#42, #44, rewire-bio/evo2-cloud-operations, rewire-bio/evo2-size-by-use-case#1) and is out of scope here.

## Decision endpoint

For a lab budgeting germline WGS: runtime, cost, peak memory, accuracy and run-to-run concordance of calls for each execution set-up, in one table from the same runs.

## Inputs

GIAB HG002 (and HG001 as a second sample) 30x Illumina WGS, plus one downsampled depth. Reference and read set pinned.

## Truth

GIAB v4.2.1 small-variant benchmark in its confident regions, scored with hap.py and the GA4GH stratifications.

## Controls and baselines

- Baseline: CPU GATK best practices (BWA-MEM and HaplotypeCaller).
- Parabricks (GPU HaplotypeCaller and DeepVariant), CPU DeepVariant.
- DRAGEN only if a licensed instance is approved in the cost quote.
- Each configuration repeated at least three times on the same instance type, and once on a second GPU type.

## Metrics

Wall time, cost at recorded list prices, peak memory, SNV and indel precision, recall and F1, pairwise call concordance between repeats and between hardware, before and after filtering.

## Data access

Public (GIAB). GPU time and any DRAGEN licence are paid, so the cost quote decides scope.

## Before any run

Literature first: check that the comparison has not been published since the review (and that no public result already answers it); run only the gaps. Then freeze a protocol (inputs, truth version, caller versions and container digests, strata, metrics, uncertainty method, failure and coverage policy) and quote hourly prices and the total cost. No run starts until the protocol is frozen and the cost is approved. Archive predictions, denominators, logs, hardware, time and memory, and deliver a result bundle to rewire-benchmark-data for review, with a clean-environment reproduction path for the article (the execution contract in #30).
title: Measure run-to-run concordance, accuracy, runtime and memory of germline WGS pipelines in one table

body:
Part of #30. Data case: rewire-bio/rewire-benchmark-data#17 (`cnv-detection-characterisation`). Article: [What six studies show about detecting and classifying copy-number variants](https://rewirebio.io/blog/what-six-studies-show-about-detecting-and-classifying-copy-number-variants/) (rewire-bio/rewire.it#384).

## Why

No comparison with per-caller values in tables covers somatic or tumour CNVs. The SEQC2 HCC1395 benchmark (Genome Biology 2024) reports caller accuracy only in figures. The germline Cue against CNVnator reproduction is owned by #40 and is not repeated here.

## Decision endpoint

Which somatic CNV caller to validate for tumour-normal genomes: per-caller recall and precision for gains and losses separately, by size.

## Inputs

SEQC2 HCC1395/HCC1395BL public WGS (and WES as a separate track), with a dilution or purity series if public reads exist.

## Truth

The SEQC2 consensus CNV call set for HCC1395, with its version and high-confidence regions. Record that the truth was built partly from the callers being tested.

## Controls and baselines

- Baseline: a read-depth caller (CNVkit for WES, Control-FREEC or CNVnator-style read depth for WGS).
- GATK somatic CNV, ASCAT or Sequenza for allele-specific calls, and any learned caller with public software.

## Metrics

Recall and precision for gains and losses separately by size bin; segment-level copy-number concordance; runtime.

## Data access

Public (SRA, SEQC2 FTP). Lower priority than #40.

## Before any run

Literature first: check that the comparison has not been published since the review (and that no public result already answers it); run only the gaps. Then freeze a protocol (inputs, truth version, caller versions and container digests, strata, metrics, uncertainty method, failure and coverage policy) and quote hourly prices and the total cost. Part of #30. Data cases: rewire-bio/rewire-benchmark-data#15 (`plasma-ctdna-fragmentomics`) and rewire-bio/rewire-benchmark-data#16 (`plasma-ctdna-methylation`). Articles: [fragmentomics review](https://rewirebio.io/blog/what-eight-studies-show-about-detecting-cancer-from-cfdna-fragmentomics/) (rewire-bio/rewire.it#382) and [methylation review](https://rewirebio.io/blog/what-seven-studies-show-about-detecting-cancer-from-plasma-dna-methylation/) (rewire-bio/rewire.it#383).

## Why

The decision endpoints for both cases (independent comparison against ichorCNA with tumour-informed tumour fraction; same-sample assay and tissue-of-origin comparisons) need controlled patient cohorts and are recorded as missing endpoints in #30. The articles still need a runnable real-data example. This issue owns that example only, as a public proxy with stated limits. It does not answer the clinical decision.

## Decision endpoint

None clinical. Proxy: on public data, does a fragment-length feature add separation over ichorCNA in a case-control set, and do reference-based deconvolution methods recover known tissue fractions in mixtures of public methylomes.

## Inputs

- Fragmentomics: public cfDNA low-pass WGS or fragment files (for example the open subsets of FinaleDB). Confirm which samples are open-access before planning; controlled cohorts (DELFI, LUCAS on EGA) are excluded.
- Methylation: public reference methylomes (Loyfer et al. 2023 atlas, GEO) mixed in silico at known fractions.

## Truth

Case or control label as published (fragmentomics); known mixing fractions (methylation).

## Controls and baselines

- Fragmentomics baseline: ichorCNA tumour fraction. Compare a fragment-length ratio feature and FinaleToolkit features, with cross-validation by source study.
- Methylation baseline: meth_atlas (least squares) and CelFiE. Hold the mixed samples out of the reference. Giuili et al. 2025 already report in silico mixtures; this is a reproduction example, not new evidence, and its values are not added as a new result.

## Metrics

AUC and sensitivity at 95% and 98% specificity with intervals (fragmentomics); absolute error in estimated fraction by fraction level (methylation).

## Data access

Public only. If no open cfDNA cohort with enough cases and controls exists, close the fragmentomics half as blocked and say so in #30.

Part of #30. Data case: rewire-bio/rewire-benchmark-data#14 (`diagnostic-rna-pathogen-detection`). Article: [RNA pathogen detection by sequencing](https://rewirebio.io/blog/rna-pathogen-detection-by-sequencing/) (rewire-bio/rewire.it#381).

## Why

No study compares RNA workflows on a spike-in or reference material, no independent comparison names the widely used workflows, and no machine-learning method has been compared with Kraken2 or Centrifuge on the same data.

## Decision endpoint

Detection sensitivity and false-positive rate for RNA viruses at low read counts, including divergent viruses, for named workflows on the same reads.

## Inputs

- Public human RNA-seq background (respiratory or blood where open, otherwise a public cell line), with simulated reads from RNA virus genomes spiked in at a dilution series.
- A divergent-virus track in which the closest reference strains are removed, mirroring the COMPARE proficiency design.
- Unspiked background as the negative control.

## Truth

Known by construction.

## Controls and baselines

- Baseline: nucleotide alignment to NCBI nt (SNAP or BLASTn as in SURPI+ and CZ ID).
- Kraken2, Centrifuge, a translated search (DIAMOND), and a virus-specific profiler.
- CZ ID on the hosted service only if the protocol allows uploading the simulated data.
- A learned classifier with public weights, if the literature check finds one that accepts reads.

## Metrics

Sensitivity by spike-in level and divergence; false-positive taxa per sample in negative controls; limit of detection in reads per million; runtime.

## Data access

All public. Prospective clinical specimens against an adjudicated composite reference need partner data and stay a missing endpoint in #30. Keep this separate from the DNA pathogen issue.

body:
Part of #30. Data case: rewire-bio/rewire-benchmark-data#13 (`diagnostic-dna-pathogen-identification`). Article: [What published comparisons show about DNA pathogen identification workflows](https://rewirebio.io/blog/what-published-comparisons-show-about-dna-pathogen-identification-workflows/) (rewire-bio/rewire.it#380).

## Why

Detection of organisms absent from the reference is tested only indirectly, and no clade-exclusion benchmark focused on pathogens has extractable values. The machine-learning classifiers (MetageNN, BERTax) are compared with the alignment baseline only in their developers' papers, at genus level or above, with no correctness endpoint for the reads they assign.

## Decision endpoint

How each workflow behaves when the pathogen is not in its reference: correct assignment at the lowest correct rank, false species-level calls, and abstention, against the alignment baseline.

## Inputs

- Simulated short and long reads from pathogen genomes (RefSeq), spiked into public human background reads at fixed fractions.
- Clade exclusion: each target species (then genus) removed from every tool's reference, using one shared database build.
- Public mock communities (for example ZymoBIOMICS) as an in-reference control.

## Truth

Known by construction: source genome and taxonomy of every simulated read.

## Controls and baselines

- Baseline: alignment to a curated reference (minimap2 with MEGAN-LR or an equivalent LCA step).
- Kraken2 with Bracken, MetaPhlAn, a protein-alignment tool (DIAMOND).
- MetageNN and BERTax using their released weights; record training overlap with the excluded clades.
- In-reference runs of the same reads as the positive control.

## Metrics

Per-read and per-sample sensitivity and precision at species and genus rank; false species calls per million reads; unassigned fraction; runtime and peak memory.

## Data access

All public. Clinical specimens against an independent reference standard need partner data and stay a missing endpoint in #30.

Part of #30. Data case: rewire-bio/rewire-benchmark-data#12 (`patient-rna-splicing-validation`). Article: [What published comparisons show about confirming splice variants in patient RNA](https://rewirebio.io/blog/what-published-comparisons-show-about-confirming-splice-variants-in-patient-rna/) (rewire-bio/rewire.it#379).

## Why

The one clinical predictor comparison on RNA-tested variants (Drost et al. 2025) covers SpliceAI, Pangolin, SPiP and SQUIRLS. No tabled comparison scores MMSplice, CADD-Splice, AbSplice, SpliceAI2 or a genomic foundation model against motif scoring on RNA-validated variants, and none reports confidence intervals.

## Decision endpoint

Which predictor to use to choose variants for RNA testing: AUROC, sensitivity and specificity at stated thresholds on variants tested in patient RNA, with intervals, against the motif-scoring baseline.

## Inputs

Variants and RNA outcomes from Drost et al. 2025 Data S1 (CC BY 4.0), plus any other public RNA-tested variant table found in the literature check. Inputs are genomic coordinates and reference only.

## Truth

RNA outcome as published (RT-PCR on patient tissue or exon trapping), kept as separate strata.

## Controls and baselines

- Baseline: motif scoring (MaxEntScan).
- SpliceAI, Pangolin (match the published configuration first, as a check against Drost), MMSplice, CADD-Splice, AbSplice (blood and fibroblast tissues), SpliceAI2 if its non-commercial licence permits, and one genomic foundation model zero-shot score.
- Record training overlap: SpliceAI2 trains on all chromosomes except 21 and 22.

## Metrics

AUROC and AUPRC with bootstrap intervals; sensitivity and specificity at literature thresholds; results by variant position (canonical, near-splice, deep intronic) and by test type.

## Data access

Public supplementary tables. Ascertainment limit: the variants were chosen for testing by clinicians, partly using predictors, which favours the predictors used; state it.

## Not in scope

The RNA-seq caller comparison (FRASER against a learned caller on patient RNA) needs controlled patient data and stays a missing endpoint in #30. Do not repeat the completed MFASS study (#19); MFASS is the reporter use case. SpliceAI2 published values are extracted in rewire-bio/rewire-benchmark-data#127 and are not rerun.

Part of #30. Data case: rewire-bio/rewire-benchmark-data#11 (`tumour-rna-fusion-detection`). Article: [What the benchmarks say about choosing an RNA fusion caller](https://rewirebio.io/blog/what-the-benchmarks-say-about-choosing-an-rna-fusion-caller/) (rewire-bio/rewire.it#378).

## Why

The main driver truth sets (Tamura et al. 2026) were selected from fusions called by at least four algorithms, so sensitivity for fusions most callers miss is not measured. No study reports intervals, and review burden is counted after manual review. Long-read precision and recall come from simulated reads only. No learned caller is compared with STAR-Fusion or Arriba on the same data.

## Decision endpoint

Which short-read caller to validate: sensitivity on fusions whose truth does not depend on caller agreement, and the number of unconfirmed calls per sample before any manual filtering, with intervals.

## Inputs

- Simulated RNA-seq with known fusions from the public STAR-Fusion benchmarking data (Haas et al. 2019).
- Public cancer cell line RNA-seq with fusions confirmed by an orthogonal assay (RT-PCR, FISH or a reference material such as Seraseq where the reads are public); the protocol lists each sample and how its truth was obtained.

## Truth

Simulated fusions (known by construction) and orthogonally confirmed fusions only. Caller-consensus truth is excluded.

## Controls and baselines

- Baseline: STAR-Fusion and Arriba.
- FusionCatcher.
- Learned or partly learned callers with public software (EricScript with its AdaBoost score; any others found in the literature check).
- A null control: shuffled or fusion-free simulated samples to count false calls.

## Metrics

Sensitivity, precision and F1 with intervals; unconfirmed calls per sample before review; sensitivity by expression level; runtime and peak memory.

## Data access

Public (Broad FTP and SRA). FFPE solid tumours against clinical assays need controlled clinical data and are out of scope; they stay a missing endpoint in #30.

Part of #30. Data case: rewire-bio/rewire-benchmark-data#10 (`tumour-dna-somatic-variant-detection`). Article: [What eight studies say about choosing a somatic variant caller](https://rewirebio.io/blog/what-eight-studies-say-about-choosing-a-somatic-variant-caller/) (rewire-bio/rewire.it#377).

## Why

The published comparisons use different truth sets, caller versions and scoring, so their values cannot be pooled. Only the HG008 preprint reports interval estimates, and only for F1. Tumour-only evidence comes from two developer papers. No study evaluates current releases of the main callers on the same public data.

## Decision endpoint

Which caller (or simple ensemble) to validate locally, given sequencing type, VAF and the normal-sample regime: per-caller precision, recall and F1 with interval estimates, stratified by VAF and variant type, in separate tumour-normal and tumour-only tracks.

## Inputs

- GIAB HG008 tumour-normal pair (public Illumina WGS).
- SEQC2 HCC1395/HCC1395BL (public WGS and WES; the FFPE and AmpliSeq libraries as a separate track if the protocol includes them).
- Depth, aligner and reference pinned.

## Truth

GIAB HG008 somatic small-variant benchmark (record the version; earlier work used draft v0.3) and SEQC2 truth set v1.2 within its high-confidence regions. HCC1395 is a training set for some released models; those models are flagged or excluded on it.

## Controls and baselines

- Baseline: Mutect2 (current GATK release), with Strelka2.
- Deep learning: DeepSomatic, ClairS, NeuSomatic (only models not trained on the evaluation sample).
- Tumour-only track: Mutect2 tumour-only, ClairS-TO, DeepSomatic tumour-only.
- Majority-vote ensemble of the tumour-normal callers.

## Metrics

Precision, recall and F1 for SNVs and indels separately, by VAF bin and by stratification region; block-bootstrap intervals; calls per Mb outside the truth set; runtime and peak memory.

## Data access

All inputs public (GIAB, SRA). Some caller licences are non-commercial; record them.

body:
The genomic foundation model guide (rewire-bio/rewire.it#401, PR #402) needs real fine-tuning times. The January guide gave a table of fine-tuning time per 10,000 samples at batch size 8 on one GPU (DNABERT-2 about 2 h, ESM-2 650M about 4 h, HyenaDNA 32k about 8 h). Those numbers had no source. This study recreates that table for the DNA models with measured values. The ESM-2 row is out of scope (protein models were dropped).

Published figures found so far are not comparable: Hegde et al. 2025 (NT-500M, 7.5 h per 5 epochs on about 89,000 variants, older GPUs) and the Nucleotide Transformer paper (20 and 50 min on a full 8x A100 node). Check Saadat and Fellay, ICLR 2026 (openreview NUleWh1GFx; PDF needs a manual download) first. Run only what it does not cover.

## Models
- DNABERT-2 117M, LoRA (the repo's own configuration: r 8, alpha 32, dropout 0.05)
- Nucleotide Transformer v2 500M, (IA)3 as in the NT paper
- HyenaDNA small 32k, full fine-tuning (the model is small enough), and LoRA if supported

## Fixed protocol (to match the January table)
- 10,000 training samples, batch size 8, one GPU
- One public sequence classification task (for example a GUE promoter task), fixed split and seed
- Same number of epochs for every model (state it), bf16 where supported
- GPUs: L4 24 GB and L40S 48 GB, using the evo2-cloud-operations harness, pinned container and price capture

## Record per model and GPU
- Wall time for the 10,000-sample run, and time per epoch
- Peak GPU memory
- Cost at recorded list price
- Test metric (MCC or AUROC) against a simple non-foundation-model baseline on the same split, so the time is tied to a working model

## Output
A table in the same shape as the January one (model, GPU, hours per 10,000 samples at batch 8, peak memory, cost), committed with run receipts. Quote hourly prices and total before launching. Results needed by 2 Nov.
title: Measure fine-tuning time and memory for DNABERT-2 and Nucleotide Transformer

body:
For the AMP 2026 talk (rewire-bio/amp-2026-talk). The audience wants a sizing table: which GPU each genomic foundation model needs, how fast it runs and what it costs. The January guide had such tables but the numbers were not sourced; they must not be reused. This study replaces them with measurements.

## Literature first
Collect published memory, throughput and hardware figures for each model (paper, model card, official repo). Run only the gaps (see `literature-first` rule).

## Models and sizes
DNABERT-2; Nucleotide Transformer v2 (500M) and 2.5B; HyenaDNA (32k and 1M context variants); Caduceus; GENA-LM; Evo 2 1B, 7B, 20B, 40B (Evo 2 7B already measured in evo2-cloud-operations). AlphaGenome only if weights can be run locally.

## Hardware
CPU, L4 24 GB, L40S 48 GB, H100 80 GB. Same harness, pinned containers and price capture as evo2-cloud-operations.

## Measure, per model, size, GPU and context length
- Peak VRAM (and OOM boundary)
- Throughput (windows or sequences per second) at a fixed workload
- Cost per 1,000 variants or sequences at recorded list prices
- Pretraining cost: from authors' stated hardware and duration only, labelled "reported", never estimated in dollars without a source

## Output
A machine-readable table plus one slide-ready figure for the talk, and a short write-up. Results must be in by 2 Nov for the 10 Nov upload. Estimated spend a few hundred USD; needs approval before runs.
title: Measure memory, throughput and cost for genomic foundation models (AMP sizing table)

body:
Part of #30 (AMP use case: CNV detection and characterisation, rewire-benchmark-data #17).

## Why

De La Vega et al. 2025 (Bioinformatics Advances) is the only published same-data comparison of a deep-learning CNV caller (Cue) against the read-depth baseline (CNVnator). Its values cannot be used: the Results text and Supplemental Table 3 disagree on whether CNVnator detected 1 to 5 kb events and on which caller had the lowest precision. The benchmark database withholds them, and the CNV review on rewirebio.io (rewire-bio/rewire.it#397) now states that there is no reliable evidence a deep-learning caller beats the baseline. Reproducing the comparison is the only way to settle it.

Nardone et al. 2025 (Biomedicines) has a related problem (read depth and aligner behind Table S1 stated inconsistently; inGAP text and table disagree) and could be covered by the same run.

## Scope

- HG002 short-read genome, depth and aligner pinned and recorded.
- Callers: CNVnator (baseline), Cue, DRAGEN CNV (CNV-only and SV-informed if licensed), Delly, Lumpy/Manta.
- Truth: GIAB HG002 SV truth set (deletions and duplications), stratified by size bin (1 to 5 kb, 5 to 10 kb, above 10 kb) and by exon overlap, matching the paper's scoring rule as closely as it is described.
- Metrics: recall, precision and F1 per size bin and event type, with the matching rule stated.
- Archive predictions, versions, container hashes, runtime and memory, per the #30 execution contract.

## Outcome

Deliver a result bundle to rewire-benchmark-data for review. If the reproduction resolves the conflict, release the values and update the CNV review's baseline section (see rewire-bio/rewire-benchmark-data#121 follow-up checklist).
title: Reproduce the Cue versus CNVnator CNV comparison on HG002 (De La Vega et al. 2025)

body:
<!-- rewire-benchmark-development-programme:2026-10-01 -->

## Purpose and scope

Track missing decision-relevant benchmark protocols, potential extensions, and conventional baseline implementation or measurement gaps across all 17 use cases. This is an execution-development backlog linked to the [article series](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/351), the [database scientific-evidence gaps](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire-benchmark-data/issues/48), and the [coverage audit in database PR80](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire-database/pull/80).

Planning reviewed 1 October 2026. PR80 was merged on 1 October 2026 after all checks passed. Production deployment is tracked in [the main-branch workflow](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire-database/actions/runs/36834130782); merge does not by itself confirm deployment. The audit found scoped evidence for every case, with remaining applicability gaps. This issue does not imply that every use case lacks an existing benchmark or that a proposed design is novel across the literature.

Distinguish four states when promoting work into a focused implementation/run issue:

- **Missing protocol or endpoint:** the intended decision is not measured by the current Rewire protocol.
- **Potential extension:** existing data or runners can support a separately registered transfer, calibration, abstention or experimental-budget question.
- **Baseline implementation/measurement gap:** a conventional method exists, but its adapter, required artifact or fair comparison on the target protocol is missing. A source-supported baseline role is not necessarily a measured baseline.
- **Evidence extraction gap:** missing tables, source conflicts, checkpoint identity, denominators or permissions need curation. These do not by themselves justify a new benchmark.

## Benchmark opportunities and first milestones

All items below are open planning work. Existing measurements remain valid within their recorded scope; completing a planning checkbox does not count as a new model run.

- [ ] **B334 — [Genetic perturbation response](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/334)** (public data protocol). Generalisation across unseen perturbations, combinations and cell contexts, with error in expression change as the primary response endpoint. **First milestone:** Freeze one Norman input/split/gene-universe manifest and run the cheap controls; register a separate context-transfer track before inspecting its outcomes.

- [ ] **B335 — [Molecular shortlisting from MS/MS](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/335)** (public data protocol). Candidate-pool and target-absence evaluation, with molecule/instrument holdouts and an explicit option to decline a nomination. **First milestone:** Reconstruct a pinned MassSpecGym-compatible retrieval track, then register new pool sizes and controlled target-removal tests.

- [ ] **B336 — [Plant promoter reporters](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/336)** (public data protocol). Promoter shortlisting across sequence groups and reporter hosts, followed by validation in the intended plant context. **First milestone:** Freeze a reporter-host-by-sequence-species protocol with sequence-group holdouts and run CPU controls before adding released model configurations.

- [ ] **B337 — [Protein variant stability](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/337)** (existing pilot then extension). Shortlist stable variants on independent proteins, keeping single and multiple substitutions in separate tracks. **First milestone:** Complete the already-planned full-assay artifact-dependent pilot; declare the article’s singles-only population separately, then register untouched proteins and a decision-endpoint protocol.

- [ ] **B338 — [Rhodopsin wavelength transfer](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/338)** (fast extension). Target-wavelength selection and calibrated uncertainty on genuinely independent sequence backgrounds. **First milestone:** Verify saved predictions/background IDs for an exploratory utility replay; register untouched backgrounds for confirmatory evaluation.

- [ ] **B339 — [Splicing follow-up](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/339)** (partner dependent). Independent gene/tissue transfer from reporter outcomes to endogenous RNA follow-up at a fixed assay capacity. **First milestone:** Reuse the MFASS harness and coverage reconciliation; identify and freeze a genuinely independent RNA-assay cohort before scoring.

- [ ] **B340 — [UTR translation](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/340)** (fast extension). Cross-library or reporter-context transfer and high-translation construct selection under a fixed experimental budget. **First milestone:** Resolve input reuse terms and complete the existing matched panel; register a cross-library split with sequence-overlap and reporter-condition checks.

- [ ] **B341 — [Rare-disease ranking at equal review effort](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/341)** (partner dependent). Measure whether adding a molecular-effect model recovers more causal findings within the same analyst-time budget. **First milestone:** Design a paired replay with solved and unresolved cases, frozen inputs, separate families/sites/time periods and explicit workload denominators; unresolved cases are not assumed negatives.

- [ ] **B342 — [Reanalysis benefit beyond updated information](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/342)** (partner dependent). Measure which unresolved cases warrant reopening and separate method benefit from new knowledge, phenotypes and calls. **First milestone:** Resolve the identified inaccessible comparison paper, then design dated cohort replay with separate method and knowledge-update arms; record diagnoses and diagnosed people separately.

- [ ] **B343 — [BRCA evidence review without more serious errors](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/343)** (expert curated). Measure whether assistance reduces complete BRCA1/2 evidence-review effort while preserving correct criteria, conflicts and uncertainty. **First milestone:** Curate frozen evidence dossiers spanning resolvable, uncertain and conflicting variants; separate calibration/evaluation variants and obtain independent hereditary-cancer adjudication.

- [ ] **B344 — [Independent somatic oncogenicity review with abstention](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/344)** (expert curated). Measure classification and reviewer utility across oncogene missense and tumour-suppressor loss-of-function mechanisms with independent references. **First milestone:** Create a representative main cohort plus a separately reported challenge set, freeze evidence, hold out studies/related allelic series and adjudicate independently.

- [ ] **B345 — [Context-sensitive EGFR evidence retrieval](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/345)** (expert curated). Measure retrieval of correctly scoped sensitivity/resistance evidence when prior therapy, treatment line, evidence date or other context changes. **First milestone:** Build a frozen public-corpus prototype with paired expert-authored scenarios, contradictions, missing context and no-supported-evidence cases; hold out studies and molecular profiles.

- [ ] **B346 — [Therapeutic target validation under a fixed experimental budget](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/346)** (partner dependent). Measure whether a nominated target shortlist yields reproducible disease-relevant benefit with selectivity. Desired cellular-state changes alone do not establish this endpoint. **First milestone:** Define one disease context, eligible targets and prespecified benefit/selectivity thresholds; freeze equal-sized shortlists, assay all nominations, and include a random reference panel. Confirm hits with orthogonal perturbations and normal-cell counter-assays.

- [ ] **B347 — [Allele–gene follow-up yield from endogenous editing](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/347)** (partner dependent). Measure whether ranked variant–gene pairs identify the allele, affected gene and cellular context worth following up experimentally. **First milestone:** Choose one edit-compatible variant class and cell context; separate development and test loci, freeze ranked pairs, and conduct blinded endogenous editing with expression and edit-efficiency measurements. Include an independently sampled reference panel.

- [ ] **B348 — [Equal-budget intervention selection for a defined cellular response](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/348)** (public data protocol). Measure how efficiently a selection policy finds perturbations achieving a prespecified cellular response while satisfying a viability constraint. Keep this endpoint separate from therapeutic validation in [#346](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/346). **First milestone:** Create a concealed, fully measured candidate panel; freeze the starting context, desired response and equal nomination budgets. Score against hidden outcomes, with a separate held-out-context track. Later add prospective evaluation.

- [ ] **B349 — [Study-transfer annotation with calibrated abstention](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/349)** (public data protocol). Measure annotation transfer to a new study or platform, including useful refusal of unsupported labels, under a common evaluation protocol. **First milestone:** Freeze ontology and reference data; hold out whole studies and platforms, include rare and reference-absent types, and tune rejection thresholds only on development studies. Score identical cells across methods.

- [ ] **B350 — [Experimental yield from protein-interface hypotheses](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire.it/issues/350)** (partner dependent). Measure whether structural predictions improve selection of informative interface mutations, rather than only predicting accurate poses. Restrict the first version to non-antibody protein–protein complexes. **First milestone:** Fix an equal mutation budget per held-out complex and assay nominated mutations for binding changes alongside expression/folding controls. Separate sequence-only and component-structure input tracks; report DockQ only as a secondary diagnostic.

## Missing baseline implementations or matched measurements

Close an item only with linked evidence from the intended protocol, including coverage and uncertainty, or a reviewed explanation that the comparator is inapplicable. Existing methods must not be marked globally absent.

## Sequence and reuse

1. **Fast protocol extensions:** Rhomax target-wavelength utility/uncertainty (B338), and UTR library transfer (B340). Complete the already-planned AMFR artifact-dependent pilot (BL337) without presenting it as a newly invented benchmark.
2. **First substantial public-data protocols:** molecular retrieval with absent candidates (B335), and study/platform annotation transfer with abstention (B349). A hidden, fully measured perturbation panel can start B348 when suitable outcomes and candidate accounting are available.
3. **Expert-curated evidence/workflow work:** context-sensitive EGFR retrieval (B345), then BRCA/somatic adjudicated review protocols (B343/B344) as reviewers become available.
4. **Partner-dependent validation:** clinical case ranking/reanalysis (B341/B342), therapeutic target validation (B346), endogenous allele editing (B347), endogenous RNA transfer (B339) and structure-guided mutation selection (B350). Prospective plant and cellular-response work also needs laboratory partners.

These development phases preserve the article-series production priorities; they do not replace the first-wave splicing, Rhomax and UTR guides.

Reuse the [current sequence benchmark integrations](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire-benchmarks/blob/01e0a50d714ab35d08519d5be2610bc37b5c1292/docs/sequence-benchmarks.md), [baseline registry](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire-benchmarks/blob/01e0a50d714ab35d08519d5be2610bc37b5c1292/packages/rewirebench/src/rewirebench/baselines.py) and evidence export contracts. The [bounded research-campaign infrastructure in draft PR24](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire-benchmarks/pull/24) is already proposed and remains unmerged; review/reuse it where appropriate.

The [MFASS annotation/masking study in issue19](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire-benchmarks/issues/19) is completed. [Issue13](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire-benchmarks/issues/13) closed the conventional-adapter implementation work; real biological measurements still require the declared external artifacts. [HPC validation issue14](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire-benchmarks/issues/14) is infrastructure validation, not a new biological benchmark.

## Evidence curation dependencies

Keep these in coordination with [database issue31](https://github.com/rewire-bio/rewire-benchmark-data/issues/48): inaccessible reanalysis comparisons/supplements; CPPC nomination denominators; source-version and numerical conflicts; exact checkpoint/split/input identity; per-model scored counts; permissions; and independent scientific review. Preserve old numerical records and archived releases. Resolve source gaps before claiming a design is absent from the literature.

## Requirements for each promoted protocol

- [ ] Assign a scientific owner and implementation owner; link a focused child issue when the bounded protocol is ready.
- [ ] Freeze the use-case decision, population/context, candidate universe, allowed inputs, endpoint and review/experimental budget.
- [ ] Record data/weight access and reuse terms, immutable artifacts, split units, pretrained-data overlap and independent test outcomes.
- [ ] Prespecify conventional controls, tuning/adaptation budgets, metrics, tie handling, missing-score/abstention accounting, uncertainty and practical effect threshold.
- [ ] Produce saved predictions, exact scored denominators, failure reasons, independently recomputed metrics and measured preparation/inference resources.
- [ ] Distinguish source-reported results, historical replay, new inference and independent prospective validation. Previously inspected test outcomes support exploratory analysis.
- [ ] Obtain appropriate independent adjudication/review. Clinical replay or synthetic scenarios do not establish diagnosis or treatment benefit; cellular-state objectives do not establish therapeutic efficacy.
- [ ] Submit reviewed records and protocol applicability to `rewire-database`, preserving existing identities; link accepted evidence and runnable examples back to the article issue.

No benchmark run, paid compute, publication or outreach is performed by creating this tracker. Each item can close with a documented, reviewed finding that an existing protocol already meets the endpoint; a negative or inconclusive comparison is also a valid outcome.
